findings.note: Last paragraph: "Under California law and San Francisco's housing code, the same conditions count as a substandard building." No ledger claim supports it (clm:1 to clm:4 are all San Francisco Housing Code 351 and say nothing about substandard buildings or California law on them). It puts a California rule and a San Francisco rule in one sentence, and "the same conditions" has no antecedent. Unsupported high-risk legal claim and a state/local blend (SR-2, SR-4). Drop the sentence, or Leo must supply the official California text (e.g. Health and Safety Code) and the official SF Housing Code text, as two separate claims, one per layer.

First paragraph: "It says nothing about any other city or county." Absence-of-law claim (SR-6) with no statute_absence claim in the ledger. Remove the sentence. If a pointer is wanted, use only: local rules vary; check with your city or county.

The unit opens with "This is a San Francisco rule, not California law." before any rule is stated, so "This" has no antecedent. Move the layer label after the rule and name it: "San Francisco Housing Code section 351 is a San Francisco rule, not California law." (clm:1 to clm:4 each carry that attribution).
